title: RTP: A Transport Protocol for Real-Time Applications
subtitle: The real-time transport protocol that carries audio and video across the Internet, powering video calls, live streaming, and VoIP.
summary: RTP carries real-time data such as audio and video over IP, usually on top of UDP. Each packet has a sequence number to spot loss and reordering, a timestamp for playback timing, and a payload type that says which format it holds. A companion protocol, RTCP, sends periodic reports about quality and who is in the session.

eli5.summary: RTP numbers every little piece of a call or video and stamps the time on it, so the receiver can put the pieces back in order and play them at the right speed.

questions: what is the rtp header format
what is an ssrc in rtp
how does rtp detect packet loss

tldr.problem: Audio and video need timing and ordering information that UDP does not give, and retransmitting late data is usually pointless.
tldr.mechanism: RTP adds a 12-byte header with a sequence number, a timestamp, a payload type and a source identifier, and RTCP sends periodic sender and receiver reports alongside.
tldr.outcome: Applications can detect loss, smooth out jitter and synchronize streams, and choose their own response. RTP still carries most real-time media.

today: RTP remains the standard way to carry real-time media. It is used in VoIP together with SIP (RFC 3261), and in WebRTC through its secure form SRTP (RFC 3711). RFC 3550 obsoleted RFC 1889 and is now STD 64, and about ten later RFCs update it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RTP provides end-to-end delivery services for data with real-time characteristics, such as audio and video. It runs over UDP and provides timestamps, sequence numbers, and payload type identification.

RTP doesn't guarantee delivery or quality - it provides the building blocks for applications to handle real-time media. Companion protocol RTCP provides feedback on quality.
sections.eli5: If you send a movie by posting a thousand postcards, each one needs a number and a time stamp so your friend can lay them out in order and show them at the right speed. That is RTP.

sections.title: RTP Packet Format
sections.content: Every RTP packet begins with a fixed 12-byte header, shown below. The first twelve octets are present in every packet; the list of contributing-source (CSRC) identifiers follows only when a mixer inserted it.
sections.eli5: Every piece starts with a small label: which piece number it is, what time it was recorded, which sender it came from, and what kind of sound or picture it holds.

sections.title: RTCP: Control Protocol
sections.content:
RTCP provides out-of-band statistics and control information for an RTP session:

Sender Report (SR)Transmission statistics from the media sender
Receiver Report (RR)Reception quality metrics (loss, jitter)
SDESSource description items (CNAME, email, etc.)
BYEIndicates a source is leaving the session
sections.eli5: RTCP is the little notes that go back and forth saying "I got most of your pieces" or "I am leaving now", so everybody knows how well the call is going.

sections.title: Applications
sections.content:
WebRTC
Browser-based real-time communication uses RTP (via SRTP) for media transport
VoIP
Voice over IP systems use RTP to carry audio between phones and PBXes
Live Streaming
RTSP-based streaming uses RTP for media delivery
Video Conferencing
Many video conferencing systems use RTP or SRTP for real-time media
sections.eli5: Whenever you talk on a video call or listen to a live broadcast, RTP-style pieces are usually what carry the sound and picture.

fields.name: Version (V)
fields.desc: Identifies the RTP version. This specification defines version 2.

fields.name: Padding (P)
fields.desc: If set, the packet ends with padding octets that are not payload; the last octet counts them.

fields.name: Extension (X)
fields.desc: If set, the fixed header is followed by exactly one header extension.

fields.name: CSRC count (CC)
fields.desc: Number of CSRC identifiers that follow the fixed header.

fields.name: Marker (M)
fields.desc: Meaning defined by a profile; intended to mark significant events such as frame boundaries.

fields.name: Payload type (PT)
fields.desc: Identifies the format of the payload. A receiver must ignore payload types it does not understand. A profile may give static codes (for example 0 = PCMU in RFC 3551) and others are agreed dynamically.

fields.name: Sequence number
fields.desc: Increments by one for each RTP data packet sent; lets the receiver detect loss and restore order. The initial value should be random.

fields.name: Timestamp
fields.desc: Sampling instant of the first octet in the packet, from a clock that increments monotonically and linearly. The initial value should be random.

fields.name: SSRC
fields.desc: Synchronization source identifier, chosen randomly so that no two sources in a session share one.

messages.label: RTP packets (seq n, n+1, n+2 ...)
messages.note: Each carries a sequence number and a sampling timestamp.

messages.label: RTCP Sender Report (SR)
messages.note: Sends sender statistics and pairs an RTP timestamp with wall-clock time.

messages.label: RTCP Receiver Report (RR)
messages.note: Reports loss, jitter and other reception quality.

messages.label: RTCP BYE
messages.note: Indicates the source is leaving the session.
